source: Cross-check of Source/COAVamp's actual C++ headers plus a real Content/ folder pass (Blueprint asset names, not just C++), against prior build notes — not a boot-test, this is a singleplayer UE5 project with no live server to boot. Re-run this diff any time new content is added to catch drift.
caveat: "Ready to test" here means the underlying asset/code is confirmed present and, for C++, compiles clean — it does NOT mean confirmed working. This matters more than usual for the Blueprint-only items below: unlike C++, a .uasset's existence can't be "compile-checked" from outside the editor, so most Blueprint-only systems are marked warn (exists, completeness/wiring unverified) even where the feature is clearly substantial, rather than good. Status values: crit = investigated but not built, or confirmed likely broken; warn = exists (C++ complete, or a real Blueprint asset set on disk) but needs in-editor verification or wiring before it's confirmed working; good = either compiles clean with nothing further needed in C++, or has a specific prior confirmation of working correctly; planned = genuinely future work — a save-data schema or field exists for it, but no actual gameplay system has been built yet, confirmed by reading the code rather than assumed. Planned items' checks are build milestones/decisions still needed, not test steps, since there's no existing behavior yet to verify. Items with a checks list can be marked tested (or, for planned items, done) behavior-by-behavior.

items.name: ACOACharacterBase / ASC wiring
items.desc: Abstract base unifying ability code across ACOAPlayerCharacter and ACOAEnemyCharacter, the two sibling classes with no other common ancestor. Declares the pure-virtual GetCOAAttributeSet() every subclass implements.

checks.label: Player character's ASC resolves correctly through ACOAPlayerState in a live PIE session
Enemy character's own ASC activates abilities correctly when AI-possessed
GetCOAAttributeSet() returns the right set on both subclasses
Abilities correctly resolve the pawn via Cast<ACOACharacterBase>(GetAvatarActorFromActorInfo())

items.name: UCOAAttributeSet
items.desc: Health/MaxHealth, Blood/MaxBlood, AttackPower, StrideCharges/MaxStrideCharges. No Stamina (removed as dead/unreferenced). No XP attribute — the existing XP/Level system stays Blueprint-only by deliberate choice.

checks.label: Health decreases correctly when a DamageEffectClass GE lands
Health/Blood correctly clamp at 0 and at their Max
Blood is spent correctly by an ability's CostEffectClass
StrideCharges increases/decreases correctly through real gameplay

items.name: UCOAGameplayAbility base + native tags
items.desc: Blueprintable/BlueprintSpawnable ability base class with an AbilityID FGameplayTag. Native gameplay tags declared in COAGameplayTags.h/.cpp under the COAGameplayTags:: namespace — no Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini used, by deliberate choice.

checks.label: A subclassed ability activates correctly from its real input binding
Native tags resolve correctly at runtime (no missing-tag warnings in the log)

items.name: Crimson Resonance (channel feed/drain)
items.desc: Channel/duration ability, polls every ~0.2s via a looping timer for interrupt conditions (target dead, escaped, out of reach), cleans up active GE handles/timer on EndAbility. Blueprint config asset: Content/Characters/ClanAssets/GA_CrimsonResonance.uasset, with GE_CR_Cooldown/GE_CR_Drain/GE_CR_HealOverTime as its GE slots.

checks.label: Channel starts correctly on activation
Interrupts correctly when the target dies, escapes, or leaves reach
Grants the Fed Recharge Buff correctly on a kill mid-channel (distinct from the target just escaping)
Cleans up GE handles/timer on EndAbility with no lingering state

items.name: Tail Lash (melee arc sweep + knockback)
items.desc: Instant fire-and-forget ability — calls EndAbility immediately after applying its effects, no channel needed. Blueprint config asset: GA_TailLash.uasset.

checks.label: Arc sweep hits every target actually inside its range
Knockback applies correctly to hit targets
Ends immediately with no lingering state between casts

items.name: Umbral Veil (stealth)
items.desc: Grants a State.Stealthed tag (Infinite-duration, no-modifier GE_UV_Stealth) for as long as the ability owns it; breaks on movement or any other ability activating. Blueprint config asset: GA_UmbralVeil.uasset.

checks.label: Grants the stealth state tag on activation
Breaks correctly on movement
Breaks correctly the instant any other ability activates

items.name: Crimson Burst (AoE lifesteal)
items.desc: Instant fire-and-forget AoE ability with a lifesteal heal back to the caster. Blueprint config asset: GA_CrimsonBurst.uasset.

checks.label: AoE correctly hits every valid target in range
Lifesteal heals the caster proportional to damage actually dealt

items.name: Umbral Chains (single-target root)
items.desc: Instant activation, delayed one-shot cleanup: zeroes the target's MaxWalkSpeed, removes the root (GE_UC_Rooted) after RootDuration via a non-looping timer built with per-activation payload state (not ability-level members, since UCOAGameplayAbility is InstancedPerActor) — a real overlapping-activation clobber bug was caught and fixed here before shipping. Blueprint config asset: GA_UmbralChains.uasset.

checks.label: Target correctly rooted (MaxWalkSpeed zeroed) on hit
Root correctly removed after RootDuration
Two overlapping activations on different targets don't clobber each other's state (regression check for the bug already fixed once)

items.name: Crimson Harvest (corpse-feed, instant)
items.desc: Instant harvest ability with an explicit OnFeedBuffEffects extension array (GE_CH_Harvested plus whatever else gets added, like the Fed Recharge buff), applied to the caster on every successful harvest. Blueprint config asset: GA_CrimsonHarvest.uasset.

checks.label: A successful harvest actually consumes/interacts with the corpse correctly
Every effect in OnFeedBuffEffects applies to the caster on a successful harvest

items.name: Phantom Stride (dash/blink) — Blueprint-only, newly found
items.desc: GA_PhantomStride + GE_Cost_PhantomStride + GE_PS_Recharge + GE_PS_SetCharges (Content/Characters/ClanAssets), spending StrideCharges via an aim-then-execute input pair (IA_StrideAim / IA_StrideExecute) with a live BP_StridePreview/M_StridePreview visual. Unlike all 6 abilities above, there is NO C++ header for this ability anywhere in Source/COAVamp/Public — it is entirely Blueprint-side, and was not present in any prior build notes for this project at all. Found only by reading the actual Content/ folder for this pass, not previously known.

checks.label: Holding IA_StrideAim shows the BP_StridePreview visual
IA_StrideExecute actually moves/dashes/teleports the player
Execution correctly spends a StrideCharge on UCOAAttributeSet
GE_PS_Recharge correctly restores charges over time
Execution is blocked/fails cleanly at 0 charges rather than going negative or erroring

items.name: "Feed to death" Stride recharge buff
items.desc: Killing a Crimson Resonance channel target, or landing a Crimson Harvest, should temporarily speed up passive Stride-charge recharge. C++ side is fully complete (GrantFedRechargeBuff(), the State.FedRechargeBoost tag, ACOAPlayerState's tag-change handler resetting recharge progress) — needs the 2 GameplayEffect assets authored and assigned in-editor before any of it can actually do anything yet.

checks.label: FedRechargeBuffEffectClass GE authored (Duration, Add modifier on StrideCharges, grants State.FedRechargeBoost)
That GE assigned into Crimson Resonance's FedRechargeBuffEffectClass slot
That GE added into Crimson Harvest's OnFeedBuffEffects array
StrideRechargeEffectClass's Ongoing Tag Requirement (Ignore State.FedRechargeBoost) added on UCOAClanDataAsset
Buff overrides normal recharge (no stacking) while active
Recharge progress resets only when the buff tag is REMOVED, not when it's added
A kill mid-channel triggers the buff; a target merely escaping/timing out does not

items.name: Enemy character types (Fey, Sevarog, Simple)
items.desc: BP_EnemyFey and BP_EnemySevarog (built on the free Paragon Fey/Sevarog character asset packs), plus a generic BP_SimpleEnemy — all under Content/Characters/Enemy. All presumably extend ACOAEnemyCharacter for real GAS/ASC support, but that inheritance, and each one's actual AI behavior, hasn't been confirmed from outside the editor.

checks.label: BP_EnemyFey actually extends ACOAEnemyCharacter (has a working ASC)
BP_EnemySevarog actually extends ACOAEnemyCharacter (has a working ASC)
BP_SimpleEnemy's actual role confirmed (test dummy vs. a real third enemy type)
All 3 take damage correctly through UCOAAttributeSet/GAS, not a separate pipeline
All 3 die/despawn/drop correctly once Health reaches 0

items.name: Inventory core (AC_InventorySystem + item data)
items.desc: The actor component AC_InventorySystem + AC_ItemDataComponent, backed by DT_ItemData and a full item-type schema (E_Itemtype/E_Quality/E_WeaponType/E_EquipmentSlot, S_ItemData/S_ArmorStatStruct/S_DamageStruct/S_HealingStruct). This is the real, live Blueprint-only system — deliberately NOT ported to the new C++ COAInventoryFunctionLibrary, since its equip/feed/interaction logic was judged too game-specific to reconstruct safely from the binary alone.

checks.label: Items add/remove correctly from the inventory
WB_InventoryGrid renders real item icons/quantities correctly
Drag-and-drop (WB_DragPreview) between inventory slots works
Item quality/type/weapon-type data reads correctly from DT_ItemData

items.name: Crafting system
items.desc: DT_CraftingRecipes + S_CraftingRecipe/S_CraftingMaterial, a real crafting queue (S_QueueSlotinfo, WB_QueueSlot) and UI (WB_CraftingPanel, WB_RecipeSlot, WB_MaterialRequirement). At least one real placeholder recipe chain exists on disk (BP_WoodStick + BP_Iron → BP_WoodSword).

checks.label: WB_CraftingPanel opens and lists real recipes from DT_CraftingRecipes
Crafting BP_WoodSword from BP_WoodStick + BP_Iron actually consumes the inputs and produces the output
The crafting queue (WB_QueueSlot) correctly processes multiple queued items in order
A missing-materials case is handled cleanly (WB_MaterialRequirement shows what's actually missing)

items.name: Equipment & gear screen
items.desc: WB_CharacterGearScreen + WB_EquippedGearSlot, backed by E_EquipmentSlot and S_ArmorStatStruct.

checks.label: Equipping an item from inventory into a gear slot works
Equipped stats (S_ArmorStatStruct) actually apply to the character
Un-equipping returns the item to inventory correctly

items.name: World storage & interaction (BP_Chest)
items.desc: BP_Chest + WB_ChestGrid, using the shared BPI_InteractInterface (via WB_InteractablewInterface) that other interactables in the project are meant to reuse.

checks.label: Opening a BP_Chest in the world shows WB_ChestGrid with its real contents
Taking an item from a chest moves it to the player's inventory correctly
The shared interact interface behaves consistently across chests and other interactables, not just this one case

items.name: COAInventoryFunctionLibrary / COAHotbarFunctionLibrary (C++ mirror)
items.desc: Native structs/logic reverse-engineered from the binary Blueprint assets above. Compiles; not yet wired into the real Blueprint graphs it's meant to eventually replace, per prior build notes.

checks.label: COAInventoryFunctionLibrary wired into the real inventory Blueprint graphs
COAHotbarFunctionLibrary wired into WB_HotbarUI/WB_HotbarSlot's graphs

items.name: Skill tree & progression UI
items.desc: DT_Skills (DataTable) + E_SkillTree enum + S_SkillInfo struct, with a WB_SkillSlot slot widget and a full WB_SkillsScreen. The native COASkillFunctionLibrary mirrors some of this logic in C++ but per prior build notes was never confirmed wired into these actual Blueprint graphs.

checks.label: WB_SkillsScreen opens and lists real skills from DT_Skills
Unlocking/leveling a skill via WB_SkillSlot actually persists (ties to the Save System's SkillTreeProgress field, previously flagged as having no confirmed live source at all)
COASkillFunctionLibrary calls actually replace the duplicated logic in these Blueprint graphs

items.name: XP/Level system (Blueprint-only, by design)
items.desc: Plain Blueprint vars on BP_ThirdPersonCharacter (CurrentXP/Level), enemy kill-reward graphs, WB_Hud's XP bar, and the save system's XPPoints/PlayerLevel fields. Owner's explicit decision (2026-08-11, reconfirming an earlier settled choice): this stays Blueprint-only permanently — NOT migrating into a real UCOAAttributeSet GAS attribute. Remaining work is confirming the existing Blueprint-only pipeline is fully wired end-to-end, not deciding an architecture.

checks.label: Enemy kill-reward graphs actually grant XP correctly
Leveling up (CurrentXP crossing the threshold) triggers correctly
WB_Hud's XP bar tracks the real Blueprint XP value live
The save system's XPPoints/PlayerLevel fields are actually wired to the real Blueprint vars, not just present in the schema

items.name: COASaveGameSubsystem (Skyrim-style, unlimited slots)
items.desc: Full replacement for the old Blueprint save system (BP_GameInstanceSavingSystem/BP_SaveGameVamp/BP_SaveManifest): SaveNewSlot/OverwriteSlot/LoadSlot/DeleteSlot/GetAllSaveSlots/GetMostRecentSaveSlot/HasAnySaveSlots, scanning Saved/SaveGames/*.sav directly via IFileManager. Compiles clean; the old Blueprint system hasn't actually been replaced/rewired in the live UI (WB_SavesScreen/WB_SaveChoicePopup/WB_SaveSlotRow) yet, and only about 8 of ~20 save fields have a confirmed live data source.

checks.label: SaveNewSlot/OverwriteSlot creates a real .sav file on disk
LoadSlot round-trips CurrentMapName/PlayerLocation/PlayerRotation correctly
Health/MaxHealth/Blood/StrideCharges/MaxStrideCharges round-trip correctly through GAS attributes on load
DeleteSlot/GetAllSaveSlots/GetMostRecentSaveSlot/HasAnySaveSlots all behave correctly against real files on disk
PruneOldAutoSaves respects MaxAutoSaves without touching quicksaves/manual saves
The real WB_SavesScreen UI actually calls the new C++ functions, not the old Blueprint ones

Restoring GAS attributes on load applies through GE_RestoreAttributes_Instant (found in Content/GAS_BPs/GamePlayEffects — a prior build note flagged this exact GE as not yet built, but a matching asset now exists on disk; confirm it's actually wired into the load flow, not just present)

Fields with no confirmed live source (XP, Level, UnlockedAbilities, SkillTreeProgress, ResonanceOverflow, AbsorbedMemories, quest/world state) are either wired to a real system now or intentionally left at defaults
WB_SaveSlotRow displays correct per-slot metadata for real saved files
WB_SaveChoicePopup (new save vs. overwrite) behaves correctly against real existing slots

items.name: HUD (WB_Hud)
items.desc: The main gameplay HUD widget — home to the Blueprint-only XP bar and other plain-Blueprint character stats, per prior build notes, alongside whatever reads from the real GAS attributes.

checks.label: Health/Blood bars on WB_Hud track real GAS attribute values live
XP bar tracks the Blueprint-only XP system correctly
HUD doesn't desync from actual character state after a level transition

items.name: Main Menu & Pause Menu
items.desc: WB_MainMenu, WB_PauseMenu, and a shared WB_ConfirmAction dialog gated by E_ConfirmActionType.

checks.label: Main menu Start correctly triggers the loading screen + Open Level travel
Pause menu opens/closes correctly mid-game via IA_Pause
WB_ConfirmAction correctly gates a real destructive action (e.g. overwrite save, quit to menu)

items.name: Notifications
items.desc: WB_NotificationToast + WB_NotificationWall, driven by E_NotifactionType/S_NoificationStruct.

checks.label: A toast notification actually appears on a real gameplay event
Multiple queued notifications stack and clear correctly on the notification wall

items.name: In-game developer console
items.desc: WB_ConsoleTerminal + WB_ConsoleLine, toggled via IA_ToggleConsole. Contents/command set entirely unknown from outside the editor — first time this system has been documented anywhere for this project; found only by reading Content/UI directly for this pass.

checks.label: Console actually toggles open/closed via IA_ToggleConsole
At least one real command executes something (confirms this isn't just a visual stub)

items.name: MiniMap
items.desc: WB_MiniMap widget backed by a real RT_MiniMap render target and M_MiniMap material — a genuine render-target implementation pattern, not just a stub. Corrects a prior build note that described this system as only "surveyed as small/low-value" — real, non-trivial assets exist for it.

checks.label: MiniMap actually renders a live top-down view, not a static image
Player position/heading indicator tracks correctly
MiniMap updates correctly across a level transition

items.name: Settings & audio mixing
items.desc: BP_GlobalSettings + 4 Sound Classes (SC_Master/SC_Dialogue/SC_Music/SC_SFX) driving WB_Settings.

checks.label: Each of the 4 volume sliders (Master/Dialogue/Music/SFX) actually changes real in-game audio
Settings persist across a relog/restart

items.name: COALoadingScreenSubsystem + native Slate widget
items.desc: Hooks the engine's global PreLoadMap/PostLoadMapWithWorld delegates via MoviePlayer, so any Open Level travel gets the loading-screen treatment automatically, no per-caller rewiring needed. Two real bugs already found and fixed in this build (a garbage-collection crash on the background texture, and a stuck-until-click auto-dismiss bug) — highest execution-risk system in the project, and NOT yet re-tested since the second fix landed.

checks.label: Loading screen shows on a normal Open Level travel (main menu Start, save-then-load)
Auto-dismisses on its own with no click needed (regression check for the fixed stuck-until-click bug)
No repeat of the background-texture GC crash across several level transitions in a row
Splash shows only on the very first level load of the session, not on later transitions
MinimumSplashDisplayTime holds its full duration even on a fast/instant boot load
BackgroundTextures array actually picks a random Altheria concept-art panel each load
Verified in Standalone Game specifically, not just embedded PIE (MoviePlayer often doesn't render in PIE at all)

items.name: Basic melee combo pipeline
items.desc: The stock UE5 "Variant_Combat" template turns out to be a much bigger self-contained system than previously known: BP_CombatCharacter/BP_CombatGameMode/BP_CombatPlayerController/BP_CombatAIController/BP_CombatEnemy, StateTree-driven AI (ChargedAttack/ComboAttack/FaceActor/FaceLocation/GetPlayerInfo/SetCharacterSpeed/WaitForLanding tasks, IsCharacterGrounded/IsInDanger conditions), EnvQuery-based targeting (Evade/Fallback/Flank), and hazard/level actors (ActivationVolume/CheckpointVolume/DamageableBox/LavaFloor) plus a UI_LifeBar. None of ACOACharacterBase/ACOAPlayerCharacter/ACOAEnemyCharacter reference Damage/Damageable/Attacker at all, meaning this entire template island most likely never touches UCOAAttributeSet::Health or GAS — could not confirm live-but-broken vs. fully dead/parallel from source alone.

checks.label: Confirm in a live test whether basic melee (BP_ThirdPersonCharacter's IA_ComboAttack) actually damages an enemy's Health at all
Confirm whether the Variant_Combat StateTree/EnvQuery AI is active on any real enemy, or is fully unused template scaffolding
If broken/dead, port basic melee into the GAS pipeline the same way GA_Melee (the Valkory clan's Blueprint ability) already does correctly

items.name: Lock-on targeting
items.desc: WB_LockOnDisplay + IA_ToggleLockOn. Unclear whether this is wired to the real GAS-driven abilities/combat, or is part of the same Variant_Combat template island as the basic melee combo above — connection status not confirmed from outside the editor.

checks.label: Toggling lock-on via IA_ToggleLockOn actually locks onto a real enemy
WB_LockOnDisplay renders correctly on the locked target
Lock-on interacts correctly with real ability targeting (e.g. Umbral Chains/Tail Lash), not just camera framing

items.name: Input & controls (keyboard/gamepad/touch)
items.desc: Full Enhanced Input setup: IMC_Default/IMC_MouseLook mapping contexts, dual keyboard+gamepad bindings for all 4 ability slots (IA_PC_Ability1-4 / IA_C_Ability1-4), plus a full touch/mobile input layer (BPI_TouchInterface, BPI_TouchInterface_Combat, UI_Thumbstick, UI_TouchSimple) — mobile support was not previously known to exist anywhere in prior build notes for this project at all.

checks.label: All 4 ability slots correctly bind to abilities on both keyboard/mouse and gamepad
Touch/mobile input layer actually works on a touch device or touch-emulation, not just present as unused assets
Camera mode/side toggles (IA_ToggleCameraMode/IA_ToggleCameraSide) work correctly

items.name: Quest system
items.desc: FCOASaveQuestData (mirroring the real Blueprint struct S_QuestData) already exists in the save schema — ActiveQuests and CompletedQuestIDs round-trip through save files today — but no actual quest-giving, tracking, or completion gameplay exists anywhere in Source/ or Content/. The data container is a placeholder waiting on the system that would populate it.

checks.label: Design the quest data flow: who gives a quest, how progress is tracked, what triggers completion
Build a quest-giver interaction (likely reusing the shared BPI_InteractInterface already used by BP_Chest)
Build a quest log/journal UI (nothing like this exists in Content/UI yet)
Wire ActiveQuests/CompletedQuestIDs to the save system for real, not just as an empty passthrough

items.name: World state / world persistence system
items.desc: FCOASaveWorldState (WorldFlags/DiscoveredLocations/HavenEstablished) round-trips through the save system, but COAPlayerCharacter.cpp's own load code has a comment stating it "has no confirmed live sink yet — not applied here." Confirmed directly from source, not inferred: nothing currently reads or writes meaningful values into these fields during gameplay.

checks.label: Decide what WorldFlags actually tracks — a generic name→bool map, or specific named flags?
Build DiscoveredLocations tracking (a natural tie-in to the MiniMap system, which already exists)
Build the HavenEstablished mechanic — sounds like a player base/home system, nothing like it exists yet
Wire the restored WorldState into actual gameplay on load, closing the gap the code comment flags today

items.name: Ability-unlock progression
items.desc: FCOASavePlayerData.UnlockedAbilities (TArray<FGameplayTag>, typed to match AbilityID on UCOAGameplayAbility) exists in the save schema, but no system currently grants/unlocks abilities progressively — all 7 abilities are presumably available from the start today. The natural tie-in is the Skill tree system (DT_Skills/WB_SkillsScreen), but that connection doesn't exist yet either.

checks.label: Design what actually unlocks an ability — a skill tree node, a level threshold, a story event?
Build the actual unlock-granting logic
Gate ability activation on UnlockedAbilities actually containing the right tag
Wire skill tree node completion to actually populate UnlockedAbilities
